segments.t: Kostya refuses to take wedding money from Nastya's father and explains that he is finishing law school. Impressed by Kostya's pride, Stepan Andreevich offers him a job as a lawyer at his factory.
Не хочешь взять деньги, тогда заработай.
Мне на заводе хороший юрист нужен.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Tell me straight, how much money do you need?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'say' and finishing on 'need'. Kostya answers right away.
'No, there is no need, I will do it myself.' In Russian, the idea of 'no' flows naturally into 'yourself' without extra filler words.
'Do you think about the future at all?' the guest raises the pitch on 'think' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'What are your plans going forward?' the guest addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'plans'. Kostya answers right away.
'I am actually finishing law school soon.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'soon'.
'Just to become a notary in some backwater?' The meaning hinges on 'so that' working together with 'backwater' in spoken Russian.
'I do not need any change at all.' the guest anchors the line on 'change', while 'need' completes the thought. Kostya answers right away.
'Excuse me, here is your change.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'excuse me' and 'here' in a few short words.
'Alright, I was mistaken then.' In Russian, the idea of 'all right' flows naturally into 'to make a mistake' without extra filler words.
'Kostya, I really want to help you.' In Russian, the idea of 'Kostya' flows naturally into 'want' without extra filler words.
Не хочешь взять деньги, тогда заработай.
'If you do not want to take money, then earn it.' the guest anchors the line on 'not', while 'to start working' completes the thought.
Мне на заводе хороший юрист нужен.

'I need a capable lawyer at my factory.' Notice how Russian expresses 'to me' and 'needed' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Не хочешь взять деньги, тогда заработай.
Мне на заводе хороший юрист нужен.
Earning real money as a lawyer sounds tempting, except that Stepan Andreevich runs a sausage factory—and Nastya is a militant vegetarian. Let us see what happens at the factory. Until next time!
